text: Ins. Co. (1989) 210 CA3d 1540, 1547-1548, 259 CR 298, 303—no coverage for emotional distress arising from employment termination; B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund, supra, 8 CA4th at 98, 9 CR2d at 907—no coverage for injuries arising from wrongful termination under policy limiting coverage to “accidents” or “occurrences”] (a) [3:358] Rationale: The concept of fortuity is basic to insurance law. There is no coverage for damages the insured expected or intended to result from its conduct. [See Waller v. Truck Ins. Exch., Inc. (1995) 11 C4th 1, 17, 44 CR2d 370, 377] (b) Application • [3:359] Minority Shareholder (a demoted executive) sued Insured for mismanaging corporate property, resulting 4 in an economic loss that caused him to suffer emotional distress which in turn caused physical injury. There was no coverage under Insured's CGL policy because there was no accidental “occurrence”; i.e., both the alleged emotional and physical distress resulted from noncovered economic losses. [Waller v. Truck Ins. Exch., Inc., supra, 11 C4th at 23, 44 CR2d at 381] [3:360 - 3:364] Reserved.
